text.p: Zurich Insurance Co confirmed it still expected 1996 results to be significantly higher than 1995, including a higher profit on investments and financial activities.

Rolf Hueppi, chairman and chief executive, said he expected continued favourable developments in operating returns in the second half of this year, but cautioned that first half profit growth could not necessarily be projected onto the rest of 1996.

"Provided there are no exceptional events in the area of claims or on the capital and foreign exchange markets, we do, however, anticipate a significantly higher overall result in the current year than that in 1995," he said on remarks preared for a news conference.
Zurich's net profit rose 32.7 percent to 576.4 million Swiss francs in the first six months of 1996 from the year ago period.
Earlier this month, Zurich had said it expected 1996 results to be significantly better than 1995.
Zurich's chief financial officer, Rolf Haenggi, said he expected positive financial results for 1996 on the basis of higher income from interest, dividends and property rents.
Haenggi noted that forecasts of financial market developments were always uncertain and that a decline on a particular closing day could always adversely affect results.
"Although this causes us to be somewaht reserved in our expectations, we are still optimistic about the (finacial) results for 1996," he said.
In the first half of 1996, Zurich's investment portfolio grew 24.2 percent to 106.9 billion Swiss francs.
Investment income rose 21.1 percent to 3.083 billion Swiss francs.
